chosen.premise: Caterpie may eat 100 leaves a day because it wants to grow up quickly.
chosen.hook: This tiny Caterpie can eat 100 leaves a day.
chosen.visualIdea: A 0.3-meter Caterpie rapidly chomps through a counter of 100 oversized leaves, then snaps into its evolution line.
chosen.note: The exact 100-leaf claim is highly surprising, concrete, and directly supported by the Pokédex; the growth motivation is also stated, though it is slightly speculative in wording.

candidates.premise: Caterpie can devour a leaf larger than its entire body right before your eyes.
candidates.hook: Caterpie eats leaves bigger than itself.
candidates.visualIdea: A tiny Caterpie is measured beside a giant leaf, then eats it from one edge until only the stem remains.
candidates.note: A clear Caterpie-specific size contradiction with excellent visual potential. It is memorable, but less distinctive than the exact 100-leaf count.

candidates.premise: At level 7, Caterpie becomes Metapod: it sheds skin, wraps itself in silk, and turns into a cocoon.
candidates.hook: At level 7, Caterpie disappears inside a cocoon.
candidates.visualIdea: A level meter hits 7; Caterpie sheds its green skin, silk spirals around it, and the silhouette resolves into Metapod.
candidates.note: Level 7 gives this a strong concrete structure and the transformation is highly visual. The evolution method comes from secondary research, and “disappears” is a dramatic paraphrase rather than a literal fact.

candidates.premise: Caterpie’s red head antenna is a chemical defense that releases a terrible stench—yet birds still eat it.
candidates.hook: Caterpie’s antenna is basically a stink bomb.
candidates.visualIdea: A red antenna flashes like an alarm, unleashing a green odor cloud at a bird silhouette—then the bird still swoops in.
candidates.note: The stink defense and ironic fact that birds still eat Caterpie are supported. Chemical-defense language is an interpretation, not a direct research phrase.

candidates.premise: Caterpie’s tiny feet use suction pads to cling to slopes, walls, trees, and any surface.
candidates.hook: Caterpie can climb walls with suction-cup feet.
candidates.visualIdea: Macro shots turn Caterpie’s feet into suction cups as it races up a wall, upside down across a branch, and up a steep slope.
candidates.note: The suction-pad detail is supported, but wall-climbing is a familiar Pokémon ability and the footage concept slightly overextends the cited evidence.

candidates.premise: Caterpie hides in foliage by matching its green body to leaves of the same color.
candidates.hook: Can you spot the Caterpie hiding in this bush?
candidates.visualIdea: A dense field of identical green leaves holds a hidden Caterpie; the camera searches before its antenna and eyes reveal it.
candidates.note: The camouflage claim is supported and easy to turn into a viewer challenge, but it lacks a sharper numerical or contradictory hook; matching leaves are inferred from the text.

rounds.request: Stronger angles would need an equally specific, well-supported contradiction or number, plus a more uniquely Caterpie-specific reveal than ordinary climbing, camouflage, or evolution.
